83dbf3ac01f347dcb82ecea7b4e3f259049662d8.summary: Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks) reports that North Korean state-sponsored group Jumpy Pisces, also tracked as Andariel and Onyx Sleet, is likely collaborating with the Play ransomware group in a 2024 incident. Jumpy Pisces gained access through a compromised user account in May 2024 and used Sliver and DTrack until early September 2024, when an unidentified actor used the same account to deploy Play ransomware. Unit 42 assesses the collaboration with moderate confidence and says it remains unclear whether Jumpy Pisces was an affiliate or an initial access broker.

subject.name: Jumpy Pisces Engages in Play Ransomware

hedges: Jumpy Pisces, or a faction of the group, is now collaborating with the Play ransomware group: believed with moderate confidence, and the report describes a likely shift in tactics.
The report assesses a degree of collaboration between Jumpy Pisces and Play Ransomware with moderate confidence.
It remains unclear whether Jumpy Pisces became an affiliate of Play ransomware or acted as an initial access broker selling network access.
Fiddling Scorpius is believed to be operating Play ransomware; some suggest it has moved to a ransomware-as-a-service model, which the group denies on its leak site.
Some suspicious files observed did not successfully execute or were not recoverable at the time of investigation.
The report describes the trend of North Korean groups joining ransomware campaigns as potential, not confirmed.
